title: Root subgroups generate a semisimple group
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed subgroups as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $\mathbf G_a$ and $\mathbf G_m$ for the additive and multiplicative group schemes [def-sc-gm-ga]. A torus is a group scheme becoming $\mathbf G_m^r$ over an algebraic closure; split means already isomorphic to this product over $F$, and maximal means maximal under inclusion. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type which is reductive, meaning that it has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup scheme. Here unipotent means that every geometric point is a unipotent matrix in a faithful linear representation. Let $T\subseteq G$ be a split maximal torus. Let $\mathfrak g$ be the tangent space of $G$ at the identity, with the action of $T$ obtained by differentiating conjugation on $G$. Let $\Phi$ be the nontrivial characters $\alpha:T\to\mathbf G_m$ occurring as weights in this action: $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ is the subspace on which $t$ acts by $\alpha(t)$. We use characters of $T$, not their differentials. Assume in addition that $G$ is semisimple, meaning that it has no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup scheme. Solvable means that successive derived subgroup schemes eventually become trivial; the derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism factors. For each $\alpha\in\Phi$, let $U_\alpha$ be the root subgroup of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. If $K\subseteq G$ is a closed subgroup scheme through which every inclusion $U_\alpha\hookrightarrow G$ factors, then $K=G$. This includes the case $\Phi=\varnothing$.

source.place: Proposition 21.49(a), printed p.439, with the root groups of Theorem 21.11(c)

proof.text: Use the character and cocharacter lattices and canonical coroots of [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] for the given split maximal torus $T$. The root-datum conventions in [lem-sfb-semisimple-roots-span] identify $Y=X_*(T)$ with the integer dual of $X=X^*(T)$ by the character/cocharacter pairing. Since $G$ is semisimple, that node gives $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}\{\alpha^\vee:\alpha\in\Phi\}=Y\otimes\mathbf Q$.

Fix $\alpha\in\Phi$ and choose $v_\alpha$ from [lem-sfb-opposite-root-sl2-parametrizations]. In $\operatorname{SL}_2(A)$ direct multiplication gives $$w(s):=x_+(s)x_-(-s^{-1})x_+(s)=sE_{12}-s^{-1}E_{21},\qquad w(s)w(1)^{-1}=h(s)$$ for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and unit $s$. Each image $v_\alpha(x_\pm(a))$ belongs to $K(A)$ by the hypotheses on $U_\alpha,U_{-\alpha}$. Closure under multiplication and inversion [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] therefore gives $\alpha^\vee(s)=v_\alpha(h(s))\in K(A)$. This is a natural factorization $\alpha^\vee:\mathbf G_m\to K$: explicitly the displayed products of the two morphisms $\mathbf G_a\to K$ and their inverses define the morphism on $\mathbf G_m$. It holds over every $A$, including nonreduced algebras.

source.place: Paragraph 21.24, p.432; matrix identity 20.41, p.423; proof of Proposition 21.49(a), p.439.

proof.text: Put $D=T\times_G K$, a closed subgroup of the split torus $T$. By [lem-sfb-split-torus-subgroups-diagonalizable], $D$ is diagonalizable. By [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality] its inclusion gives a surjection $q:X^*(T)\to X^*(D)$. Step 2 makes every canonical coroot factor through $D$. If $\chi\in\ker q$, then $\chi$ restricts trivially to $D$, so $\langle\chi,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$ for every $\alpha$. The rational spanning and perfect pairing of Step 1 imply $\chi=0$ (the character lattice is free abelian). Thus $q$ is an isomorphism; the same contravariant equivalence makes $D\hookrightarrow T$ an isomorphism. Consequently $T\hookrightarrow G$ factors through $K$. This uses no assertion that a coroot is primitive, and remains valid when the lattice index is divisible by the characteristic.

source.place: Proposition 21.49(a), p.439, final lattice-duality sentence, expanded using Theorem 12.9(a), pp.233--234.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], the finite root decomposition is $\operatorname{Lie}(G)=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi}\mathfrak g_\alpha$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations], each $U_\alpha$ is smooth and connected with tangent space $\mathfrak g_\alpha$. The split torus $T$ is smooth and connected by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-subgroup-tangent-generation] to the finite family consisting of $T$ and the $U_\alpha$. Their tangent spaces span, all factor through $K$, and $G$ is smooth connected affine of finite type. It follows that $K=G$.

source.place: Theorem 21.11(f) and its proof, pp.429--430, using Corollary 10.17, p.191; Proposition 21.49(a), p.439.

proof.text: If $\Phi=\varnothing$, Step 1 gives $Y\otimes\mathbf Q=0$. Since $T$ is split, its free character lattice has rank zero and $T$ is the trivial group. Step 3 still applies with no coroots: the perfect pairing forces $\ker q=0$. Step 4 then applies to the singleton family $\{T\}$; its tangent space is all of $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ by the root decomposition. Thus the same conclusion includes the asserted empty-root case.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 21.49(a), printed p.439; Theorem 21.11(f), printed pp.429--430; the torus inclusion is expanded by character antiduality rather than inferred only from points.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q108-006d9f548 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: First delivery: live and side-live still have the item unsplit, there is no repair note, and the item's statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. Source read: Milne 21.49(a) p.439, 21.11 with its proof pp.428-430, 21.24 p.432 and 10.15-10.17 p.191. The proof follows 21.49(a) for an arbitrary closed subgroup scheme K, with two expansions: Milne's 'by duality' becomes an explicit character argument, and 21.11(f) is replaced by the tangent-generation lemma applied directly to K. Step 1 takes the coroot span of Y⊗Q (semisimple-roots-span) and the perfect pairing; steps 2 and 3 use the same borel-pair coroots. Step 2: I multiplied the matrices by hand; x+(s)x-(-1/s)x+(s) = sE12 - s^-1E21 and w(s)w(1)^-1 = diag(s,s^-1) hold over every algebra A. The subgroup property of K(A) then gives the factorization alpha^vee: G_m -> K by Yoneda, also for nonreduced A. Step 3: D = T x_G K is diagonalizable, antiduality makes q: X(T) -> X(D) surjective, and ker q pairs to 0 with every coroot, so ker q = 0 by the span, the perfect pairing and torsion-freeness. Hence D = T and T is in K; no primitivity of coroots is used (PGL2 in characteristic 2 is fine). Step 4: Lie(G) = Lie(T) + sum of g_alpha, T and the U_alpha are smooth and connected, and the new lemma gives K = G. Step 5 (Phi empty): G is trivial, correct. New node lem-sfb-opposite-root-sl2-parametrizations is exactly Milne 21.11(b),(e) with 21.24, which states U- -> U_{-alpha} is an isomorphism; I checked the weight signs, SL2 and PGL2. It is not a duplicate: rank-one-reflections gives only the upper restriction. New node lem-sfb-smooth-subgroup-tangent-generation is Milne 10.17 with stronger hypotheses, so it is true: the smooth generated subgroup is contained in K and 10.15 gives equality. The empty family is fine and alpha_p is excluded because the H_i must be smooth. The only DAG analogues (lem-wf-same-lie-closed-subgroup, lem-ag-equal-dimension-subgroup) are characteristic-zero Q̄_ℓ statements, so not duplicates. All proof_deps are on-unit (sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability) or definitions, no SGA, and the searches are recorded.
